newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU air alliances legislation plan delayed one week.
newsitem.headline: EU air alliances legislation plan delayed one week.

text.p: A European Commission proposal to gain clear and undisputable jurisdiction over alliances between EU and non-EU airlines has been delayed by a week, Commission officials said on Wednesday.
The proposal made by European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert will become effective by May 16 if no objections are raised by his colleagues, the officials said.
It was slated for approval by Wednesday, but the deadline was extended mainly because of bank holidays in May which led to many officials being away, they said.
The Commission wants to amend existing legislation which gives it power to ensure fair competition in air transport services between EU airports only.

The move is aimed at avoiding future battles with national governments over the legal competence to vet deals similar to those announced last year between British Airways and AMR Corp's American Airlines, and KLM Royal Dutch Airlines and Northwest Airlines Inc.

By gaining authority over services with non-EU airports the Commission may also get to rule on a vast network of bilateral commercial agreements on tariffs and capacity which airlines have entered into under the auspices of their own governments, one lawyer said.

It is not the first time the Commission has tried to gain full authority over international alliances and agreements between EU and non-EU airlines. An attempt in 1989 ran into opposition from almost all EU states.
Commission officials and European anti-trust experts think it might stand a better chance now as transatlantic deals have mushroomed, raising fears that fair competition and consumers might lose out.
EU institutions are closed on Thursday (Ascension Day) and Friday, for Schumann Day, celebrating the former French minister's role in launching the European integration movement.
